test: T62 stage 2 supporting record: worker tool-call behaviour per arm
derived_from: CodeBuddy job transcripts at the local service
note: Supporting data behind T62-stage2-real-project.json. Raw transcripts are not committed (they contain absolute workspace paths); this file keeps only counts, file names and the commands that matter to the memory question.

B.note: This run committed into the project root instead of the worker worktree, so the Verifier rejected it (head unchanged). Preserved as the rejected_b_run; the accepted B is a separate attempt.

observed_difference.extra_read_in_memory_free_arm: C0 additionally read tests/test_parsing.py (+1 read, +1 tool call)
observed_difference.interpretation: One sample. The memory arm explored one file less, which is consistent with the injected rule explaining the parser/metrics relationship, but a single paired run cannot establish that this is caused by memory rather than by sampling noise in the Worker.

behaviour_probe.method: same script executed against each arm's worktree source tree
behaviour_probe.conclusion: The two implementations are observationally equivalent on the probed inputs; C1's patch is shorter (35 vs 50 added lines) but this run does not show a behavioural advantage.
